appraisal_events.evidence: il avait fait, pour une phase nouvelle de sa vie, honorée, glorieuse, une apparition de grand homme... il paraissait un de ces hommes de talent qui à toute époque ont fleuri dans le grand monde et on ne pensait pas qu'il eût jamais vécu ailleurs.
appraisal_events.explanation: Society, especially the young, now treats Bloch as a naturally eminent, talented figure of the great world, but the narrator frames this reputation as resting on unoriginal work and collective forgetting of his earlier, humbler life.

appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch était entré en sautant comme une hyène... se tenait le visage presque effrayant, tout anxieux, d'un vieux Shylock attendant, tout grimé dans la coulisse, le moment d'entrer en scène... À quoi cela l'avançait-il?
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's own direct perception undercuts Bloch's social triumph, describing him with predatory-animal and anxious, aging-actor imagery and pointedly questioning what his advancement is worth given his nearness to death.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch has gained real entree and standing in high society that he previously lacked, even though the narrator questions the basis of this new reputation.
The narrator's private, visceral description sharply lowers Bloch's dignity, likening him to a hyena and to an anxious, aging performer nearing death.

ambiguities: Bloch's social ascension (E1) is presented as society's ironized, forgetting-based view rather than the narrator's endorsed judgment, while the narrator's own direct diminishment (E2) runs in the opposite direction in the same passage; the two registers coexist without resolving into a single verdict on Bloch.
